title: A finite free model from finite top cohomology of approximation cones
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, and fix a universe v in which R is small. Let C be a cochain complex of R-modules in universe v, with image Q(C) in the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Fix an integer b and suppose H^i(C)=0 for i>b. Suppose moreover that for every bounded complex F of finite free R-modules, every chain map f:F to C and every integer n, if H^i(Cone(f))=0 for i>n, then H^n(Cone(f)) is a finite R-module. Then there is a cochain complex P of finite free R-modules with P^i=0 for i>b and a chain-level quasi-isomorphism P to C. Here Cone(f)^i = F^(i+1) direct sum C^i, with its usual mapping-cone differential; all modules, complexes and maps are in the same fixed universe v.

source.place: Tag 064U, proof of (2) implies (1), descending finite-free construction after finite cone cohomology is established; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/064U

proof.text: At n=b+1 choose F=0 and its zero map to C; it is zero above b and below n, induces cohomology isomorphisms for i>n and a surjection at n. Suppose such a stage F to C is constructed. In the cone long exact sequence, surjectivity at n and the isomorphisms above n show H^i(Cone(f))=0 for i>=n. The hypothesis therefore makes H^(n-1)(Cone(f)) finite.

Choose a finite list of generating cohomology classes of Cone(f) in degree n-1, and representatives (a_j,c_j) that are cone cycles. Their equations are d_F(a_j)=0 and f(a_j)+d_C(c_j)=0, with the mapping-cone signs. In degree n-1 adjoin a finite free module on this list, taking its differential to F^n to be the a_j and its map to C^(n-1) to be -c_j (or the equivalent signs in the chosen cone convention). The cycle equations prove d squared is zero and the chain-map equation. These terms fit in v because R is small. In the long exact sequence, the image of these classes covers the kernel of H^n(F) to H^n(C). Adjoining them makes H^n an isomorphism. To see surjectivity at n-1, represent a class in H^(n-1)(C) by a cycle c and express the cone class (0,c) as a linear combination of the chosen classes modulo a boundary. Since the original F is zero below n, the F component of that boundary is zero. Thus the same coefficients on the new basis yield a cycle in the new F^(n-1) whose image is c modulo a C-boundary. This proves surjectivity and completes the extension without changing the degrees at least n.

Use dependent choice on k in the natural numbers to choose these compatible extensions at n=b+1-k. Define the final degree-i module from the stage when degree i is first added, and its map and differential from the stage when all their components have stabilized; transport along the compatibility identifications. The differential identities hold because they hold at a common finite stage. Terms above b remain zero and every other term is finite free. For each i the three terms in degrees i-1,i,i+1 and the map to C have stabilized once the stage passes below i. That stage induces an isomorphism on H^i, so the final map does too. It is a quasi-isomorphism.

theorem exists_finiteFree_model_of_finite_cones (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Small.{v} R]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{v} R)]
    (C : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) ℤ) (b : ℤ)
    (hvan : ∀ i : ℤ, b < i →
      IsZero ((homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) i).obj (Q.obj C)))
    (hcone : ∀ (F : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) ℤ) (a c : ℤ),
      F.IsStrictlyGE a → F.IsStrictlyLE c →
      (∀ i : ℤ, Module.Free R (F.X i) ∧ Module.Finite R (F.X i)) →
      ∀ (f : F ⟶ C) (n : ℤ),
        (∀ i : ℤ, n < i → IsZero
          ((homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) i).obj (Q.obj (CochainComplex.mappingCone f)))) →
        Module.Finite R
          ((homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) n).obj (Q.obj (CochainComplex.mappingCone f)))) :
    ∃ (F : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) ℤ), F.IsStrictlyLE b ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, Module.Free R (F.X i) ∧ Module.Finite R (F.X i)) ∧
      ∃ f : F ⟶ C, QuasiIso f
